sections.title: ZHAW Institute of Information Systems (IWI)
facts: Combines business administration and computer science to integrate AI and digital technologies responsibly into organisations with clear added value.

Expertise includes data science, data-driven business models, process science and automation, information-system design, human-centred cybersecurity, IT management, digital strategies, virtual reality and social robotics. Applied research, continuing education and knowledge transfer connect academia and industry.

sections.title: Socially Intelligent and Responsible Agents (SIRA) Lab
facts: Part of ZHAW's IWI. Studies how digital agents perceive social signals, structure behaviour transparently and create responsible value for individuals and groups through human-AI collaboration.

Investigates embodiment, perception/behaviour, social topology, temporal structure, participating actors and depth of social modelling; combinations are experimentally evaluated for social adaptation, responsibility and usefulness.

The lab develops PROMETHEUS for rapid prototyping and experimental validation of multimodal digital agents, including avatars and physical embodiments, using explicit interaction control and structured behaviour plans.

sections.title: Prof. Dr. Theresa Schmiedel
facts: Head of ZHAW's Institute of Information Systems (IWI), according to the 20 October 2026 briefing.

sections.title: Marc Styger
facts: The SIRA Lab computer scientist responsible for all code the lab develops for its Unitree G1 robot.

sections.title: Jasmin Grassmugg
facts: The SIRA Lab Robot Operator & Robot Show Designer.

sections.title: Alexandre de Spindler
facts: Helps direct the SIRA Lab; this describes his role, not a confirmed formal Director title.
An applied researcher and interactive-system designer with over two decades of experience in information systems, human-computer interaction, human-AI collaboration and applied innovation.

His work includes PROMISE (stateful prompt orchestration), Social Behaviour Regulation (socially adaptive tone, timing and participation) and PROMETHEUS (structured multimodal interaction). Methods include participatory design, prototyping and real-world evaluation with implementation partners.
Since 2010 he has led or co-led applied projects supported by Innosuisse, DIZH, the EU AAL programme and other Swiss funds, including healthcare, education, teamwork and digital services.
